narrative.overview: This landing page treats the course announcement as a useful printed prospectus. The visitor should feel they have opened an issue with a date, a sequence, an index, a calendar, a fee ledger, and a reliable way to ask for a place. The page earns attention through editorial rhythm and source-backed specificity rather than a decorative dashboard or a collection of promotional cards.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper, dark ink, and one oxidized vermilion accent.
Source Serif 4 for the title and course voice, IBM Plex Sans for readable body copy, and IBM Plex Mono for codes, dates, and fee columns.
Hairline rules, ruled rows, and asymmetric columns replace rounded card grids.
A single masthead entrance motion; content is visible by default and reduced motion is respected.
The registration state is honest: contact links work, while the missing official QR and form link are named plainly.

rules.name: The Cool Paper Rule
rules.body: Keep the background cool and quiet, like an archival sheet under daylight. Use the deeper paper only to separate bands; never add a gradient.

rules.name: The Single Accent Rule
rules.body: Vermilion is reserved for the active registration action, source identifiers, dates, and small status marks. Do not introduce a second accent color.

rules.name: The Editorial Scale Rule
rules.body: Source Serif 4 carries the title, section heads, course names, and people names. IBM Plex Sans carries paragraphs. IBM Plex Mono is reserved for codes, dates, labels, and money. Keep body measure near 65 to 75 characters.

rules.name: The Index Before the Pitch Rule
rules.body: The first viewport must answer what the course is, when it happens, and how to continue reading. Use a masthead and factual dossier before longer explanation.

rules.name: The Ruled Sequence Rule
rules.body: Repeatable course information belongs in aligned rows and a calendar sheet, not same-size feature cards. At small widths, rows become a single readable column in the same order.

dos: Do use real notice numbers, course codes, dates, fees, contact numbers, and the source's missing-link state.
Do keep the CEA audience paired with the CEA course and the time-series audience paired with the time-series course.
Do keep the mobile order identical to the reading order.
Do use visible focus states and close the mobile menu on Escape, outside click, or link activation.
donts: Don't add decorative charts, fabricated metrics, stock imagery, generic icon tiles, gradients, glass, pills, or equal feature cards.
Don't imply that a registration form or QR code exists before the organizer supplies it.
Don't place unsupported outcomes, prices, testimonials, or credentials in the page.
